candidate.scope: standalone prequantized diagnostic only; never model-routed
candidate.design: Two wave32 groups retain the production 64-output x 32-row block geometry. Each consumes GGML-compatible Q8_1 activation blocks and signed Q8T16 payload through RDNA3 integer WMMA, scales every 32-K integer dot into FP32, and writes BF16.

correctness.red: Collection failed because no prequantized Q8_1 x Q8T16 integer-WMMA wrapper or registry key existed.
correctness.green_command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-lcp3.txt PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/test_gguf_q8_0_t16_wmma_prefill.py -q -k lcp3b
correctness.note: The initial implementation used the WMMA output lane's input-load row scale and failed relative L2 around 0.24-0.27. Correctly indexing the scale by each accumulator output row fixed both ordinary and tail fixtures before timing.

microbench.protocol: W7900 HIP events, eight cycling Q8T16 weight copies, three warmup cycles, 60 rotated measured repetitions per mode, cached builds. The prequantized body and quantization-included legs use the existing GGML-compatible BF16-to-Q8_1 kernel.

decision.reason: The prequantized integer-WMMA body itself is 44.66% slower; Q8_1 quantization adds only 0.016 ms and is not the blocker. Directly packing the current K-major T16 payload and scaling every 32-K dot does not reproduce llama.cpp MMQ's tiled shared-layout economy.
decision.profiler: Skipped after the predeclared primary body gate failed.
decision.source_disposition: Remove candidate kernel, wrapper, key, and tests; production source/defaults remain unchanged.
decision.next: Do not route the existing raw-sidecar dp4a diagnostics or this direct T16 body. Any further dense-Q8 attempt must first reproduce the actual llama.cpp Q8_1 MMQ shared tile/decomposition in a standalone microbenchmark or identify a different exact body-level bottleneck.
